sections.h2: Where is Easley, SC, and what county is it in?
sections.html:
Easley is in southeastern Pickens County, with a small part in Anderson County, about 12 miles west of central Greenville. It sits at roughly 1,011 feet of elevation.

The city is compact, at about 13 square miles, and it has grown steadily. The population was 17,754 in 2000, 19,993 in 2010 and 22,921 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 27,319.

sections.h2: How did Easley start, and why does it still look like a mill-era town?
sections.html:
Easley grew up around the railroad and the textile industry. The town is named for William King Easley, and the Atlanta and Charlotte Air Line Railway was routed through the area after local backers raised $100,000. The Pickensville post office became Easley's in 1875.

Textiles drove growth after the railroad arrived, and the Easley Textile Company, later Swirl Inc., came in 1953. Construction of U.S. Route 123 later helped bring retail and new businesses. A town with a railroad-era start and a 1953 mill arrival has houses of many ages, so ask your inspector about the age of the wiring, plumbing and roof.

sections.h2: What do people in Easley do for work and school?
sections.html:
Easley is close to Greenville, and within the city the military has a presence through an Army Air Missile Defense battery at the National Guard Armory plus Army and Marine Corps recruiting offices.

The Pickens County portion of the city is served by the School District of Pickens County, including Easley High School and R.H. Gettys Middle School, plus five elementary schools. The Anderson County portion is served by Anderson School District 1.

Tri-County Technical College has a campus in Easley, and Clemson University and Southern Wesleyan University are nearby, along with Greenville Technical College and Furman University in Greenville. The Pickens County Library System has a branch in town.

sections.h2: What events and places shape how Easley feels to a buyer?
sections.html:
Easley hosts youth baseball and a state fair, which bring visitors each year. It held the Big League World Series from 2001 to 2016, and the Senior League World Series has been played there since 2017. The Upper South Carolina State Fair is held annually in early September.

In 2023, Lisa Talbert became the first woman to serve as Easley's mayor.

sections.h2: What rules does the City of Easley apply to repairs and permits?
sections.html:
Easley requires building permits for structures of 200 square feet or more, and for any size of work that includes plumbing or electrical. The city's FAQ page lists the points sellers hit most often:

  • Remodels need a permit when they change the structure or involve electrical, plumbing or mechanical work.
  • Detached structures are capped at 800 square feet and 15 feet in height.
  • Front-yard fences are limited to 4 feet and need Public Works approval at 864-855-7916.
  • A home should not be occupied before a Certificate of Occupancy is issued.
  • Vehicles stored on a property must be fully covered by a factory-made car cover.

Planning and Development handles zoning and permit applications at Easley City Hall, 205 North First Street, phone (864) 855-7908. Code Enforcement is a separate department. The city's FAQ page has the details. If you have unpermitted work, ask the city before a buyer finds it.

The city's FAQ page links to Easley Combined Utilities, Blue Ridge Electric Cooperative and the Fort Hill Natural Gas Authority. Which provider serves a house depends on the street, so the seller should know which accounts to close out at the sale.

Transfers of service are usually simple, but confirm the final read date with each provider so the closing statement is accurate.

sections.h2: How does a property tax appeal work in Pickens County?
sections.html:
Pickens County reappraises all property once every five years, and appeals must be filed within 90 days of the notice date. The assessor's FAQ describes the 2019 reappraisal, which used a December 31, 2018 effective date, and says values stay the same for four years unless a sale, new improvement, exemption change or successful appeal changes them. Ask the assessor which cycle applies to you now.

Owner-occupied homes are assessed at 4 percent, and non-owner-occupied property at 6 percent. The application can be filed any time before the January 15 penalty date, and losing eligibility has to be reported or a penalty of 100 percent of the tax can apply. The County Board of Assessment Appeals hears disputes. See the Pickens County Assessor FAQ.

  • Real property (Assessor): (864) 898-5872
  • Homestead exemption (Auditor): (864) 898-5895
  • Tax payments (Treasurer): (864) 898-5883
  • Delinquent taxes: (864) 898-5890

After a sale, the owner on December 31 is liable for that year's tax, though the new owner should receive the bill. Settle this on the closing statement.

sections.h2: How does Pickens County set the value on an Easley house?
sections.html:
The Assessor uses three approaches: market (recent comparable sales, the main method for homes), cost (replacement cost minus depreciation, plus land) and income (for property that earns rent). Residential values come from mass appraisal using statistical models of arm's-length sales.

Square footage is taken from exterior measurements, which may differ from the builder's or an agent's figures. If your listing sheet and the county record disagree, that is worth correcting before a buyer notices.

The County Auditor usually mails real property tax bills in September. Tax equals taxable value times the assessment rate times the mill levy divided by 1,000. Local taxing bodies, not the Assessor, set the mill levy, so a bill can rise even when the assessment does not. If your mortgage company pays the taxes, forward any bill you receive to them.

sections.h2: How does a business license or rental fit into an Easley sale?
sections.html:
Easley requires a business license for new businesses and relocations, applied for through the Business License Department at City Hall, and a business license inspection must pass before the license is issued. A buyer who plans to run a business from the property should check that and the zoning in the city's Unified Development Ordinance first.

The Planning and Development department manages the ordinance, the zoning map, and applications for rezoning, annexation, variances and zoning clearance. Sellers with an unusual lot, a detached building or a home business should ask for a zoning clearance before they list.

sections.h2: What do Easley sellers usually need to decide?
sections.html: An Easley seller can list the house, sell it directly, or take a cash offer. Houses that need permits, repairs or a quick close are the ones where a cash sale tends to fit. Collect your payoff figure, tax bill and any permit records first, and compare the routes with a clear head.

faqs.q: What county is Easley, SC, in?
faqs.a: Easley is mostly in Pickens County, with a small part in Anderson County. The assessor and treasurer you use depend on which county the parcel is in.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Pickens County assessment?
faqs.a: Appeals must be filed within 90 days of the notice date, and filing does not delay your payment deadline. Include comparable sales, appraisals or repair estimates with the appeal.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair my Easley house before selling?
faqs.a: Yes, for structural changes and for any plumbing, electrical or mechanical work, and for structures of 200 square feet or more. Call Planning and Development at (864) 855-7908 before starting.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax when an Easley house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The owner on December 31 is liable for that year's tax, but the new owner should get the bill. The closing statement usually prorates it between buyer and seller.
The city links to Easley Combined Utilities, Blue Ridge Electric Cooperative and Fort Hill Natural Gas Authority. Check your bills to see which apply.
